{"idea":"Use the subtraction equation to write m = n + 2. Then bound n on either side of 16; the product equation rules out both n ≤ 15 and n ≥ 17.","proof":"  have hle : n ≤ m := by
    by_contra h
    have hlt : m < n := Nat.lt_of_not_ge h
    have hz : m - n = 0 := Nat.sub_eq_zero_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt hlt)
    rw [hz] at h₂
    norm_num at h₂
  have hm : m = n + 2 := by
    have ht := Nat.sub_add_cancel hle
    rw [h₂] at ht
    nlinarith
  by_cases hn : n ≤ 16
  · by_cases he : n = 16
    · nlinarith
    · have hn15 : n ≤ 15 := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (lt_of_le_of_ne hn he)
      have hp : n * n ≤ 15 * 15 := Nat.mul_le_mul hn15 hn15
      nlinarith
  · have hn17 : 17 ≤ n := Nat.lt_of_not_ge hn
    have hp : 17 * 17 ≤ n * n := Nat.mul_le_mul hn17 hn17
    nlinarith","insight_statement":"m = n + 2","insight_proof":"  have hle : n ≤ m := by
    by_contra h
    have hlt : m < n := Nat.lt_of_not_ge h
    have hz : m - n = 0 := Nat.sub_eq_zero_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt hlt)
    rw [hz] at h₂
    norm_num at h₂
  have ht := Nat.sub_add_cancel hle
  rw [h₂] at ht
  nlinarith"}
